title: Advanced SQL and Database Engineering Laboratory
description: PostgreSQL-focused progression from relational design to advanced healthcare analytics, performance, security and operational handoff.

challenges.title: PostgreSQL setup and connection
challenges.scenario: Install or start PostgreSQL, create a dedicated training database, connect with DBeaver or psql, and inspect server/database versions.
challenges.tasks: Install PostgreSQL using the platform guide. Create database hda_training. Connect using a dedicated role, not the postgres superuser for routine work. Record server_version, current_database(), current_user and connection settings.
challenges.acceptance: A successful connection returns the server version, hda_training as the database, and the intended least-privilege role.
challenges.safety: Do not expose a database port publicly. Use localhost for training.

challenges.title: Relational design and normalisation
challenges.scenario: Convert a denormalised medication-order sheet into encounter, department, drug and order entities. Explain 1NF, 2NF and 3NF.
challenges.tasks: Identify repeating groups and update anomalies. Define primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints, NOT NULL and CHECK constraints. Explain why encounter facts and order facts have different grains.
challenges.starter: See schema.sql and normalisation-exercise.md. Build the four core tables and document each table's grain.
challenges.acceptance: Four tables have stable primary keys; each medication order references one encounter and one drug; department is not duplicated as free text in every order.
challenges.safety: A normalised design reduces update anomalies; it does not automatically make every analytical query faster.

challenges.title: Types, constraints and safe schema creation
challenges.scenario: Create a PostgreSQL schema with appropriate data types and defensible constraints.
challenges.tasks: Run schema.sql then seed.sql. Inspect information_schema.columns and pg_constraint. Explain DATE vs TIMESTAMP, NUMERIC vs FLOAT, BOOLEAN and generated identity keys.
challenges.starter:
SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_schema='hda'
ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position;
challenges.acceptance: All tables exist in schema hda; constraints reject invalid values such as negative quantity and invalid length of stay.
challenges.safety: Use NUMERIC for currency-like values. Avoid storing dates as formatted text.

challenges.title: Advanced SQL patterns
challenges.scenario: Use joins, anti-joins, correlated subqueries, CTEs, window functions and set operations to answer healthcare questions.
challenges.tasks: Calculate department activity, identify encounters with no orders, rank drug classes, compare each department with the overall average and combine two compatible cohorts.
challenges.starter: Run challenges.sql sections 04A–04E and compare with solutions.sql.
challenges.acceptance: Results preserve declared grain. LEFT JOIN retains encounters without orders. Window calculations do not accidentally multiply encounter counts.
challenges.safety: Always state the denominator and grain before writing a query.

challenges.title: Healthcare cohort and medication utilisation
challenges.scenario: Create a reproducible cohort and calculate medication-order utilisation metrics.
challenges.tasks: Define inclusion dates and encounter types. Calculate orders per encounter, distinct drugs, therapeutic-class mix, department variation and a supplied readmission-flag proportion. State that order records do not prove administration or adherence.
challenges.starter: Run solutions.sql section PG-05. Reconcile counts against the data dictionary.
challenges.acceptance: 80 encounters and 150 orders in the packaged seed data; 70 encounters have at least one order and 10 have none; supplied readmission flag 7/80 = 8.75%.
challenges.safety: The readmission flag is synthetic and unvalidated. It is not a clinically validated outcome.

challenges.title: Indexes and query performance
challenges.scenario: Use EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), understand B-tree indexes and evaluate composite and partial indexes.
challenges.tasks: Capture a baseline plan, create an index, rerun the query and compare estimated/actual rows and execution time. Explain why small synthetic tables may still use sequential scans.
challenges.starter: Run performance-lab.sql. Test a selective predicate on medication_orders and inspect pg_indexes.
challenges.acceptance: You can explain plan nodes, estimated vs actual rows, scan choice and index selectivity without claiming an index always improves performance.
challenges.safety: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query. Do not use it casually on expensive production statements.

challenges.title: Views, functions, triggers and transactions
challenges.scenario: Create a reporting view, a materialized view, a safe PL/pgSQL function, a validation trigger and transaction examples.
challenges.tasks: Create view v_department_summary. Refresh the materialized view after seed changes. Test a function and trigger in a transaction, then ROLLBACK. Explain ACID, isolation and locking at a conceptual level.
challenges.starter: Run objects-and-transactions.sql in a disposable training database. Inspect pg_views and pg_matviews.
challenges.acceptance: View definitions are queryable; materialized view refresh works; trigger rejects invalid order quantity; rollback leaves no test row.
challenges.safety: Do not use triggers to hide business logic or silently rewrite clinical data.

challenges.title: Security, backup, restore and migrations
challenges.scenario: Apply least privilege, create a read-only analyst role, use pg_dump/pg_restore, and plan a controlled schema migration.
challenges.tasks: Create analyst_readonly with SELECT-only grants. Verify write denial. Export a custom-format backup, restore to a new database and compare row counts. Write a migration with forward and rollback notes.
challenges.starter: Follow security-backup-lab.md and platform commands. Use local-only credentials via environment variables or a password manager.
challenges.acceptance: Read-only role can SELECT but cannot INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Backup restores into a clean database and row counts reconcile.
challenges.safety: Never commit passwords, connection strings with secrets, or identifiable patient data.

challenges.title: Python application access and parameterised queries
challenges.scenario: Connect Python to PostgreSQL with psycopg and use bound parameters, transactions and safe error handling.
challenges.tasks: Create a virtual environment, install requirements-postgresql.txt, configure environment variables and run postgres_connection_demo.py. Compare safe parameter binding with unsafe string concatenation.
challenges.starter: Run the Python demo against the local hda_training database.
challenges.acceptance: Connection succeeds; parameterised query returns a bounded result; no password is embedded in source code.
challenges.safety: Parameterisation prevents SQL injection in values. Identifiers need safe allow-listing or psycopg SQL composition.

challenges.title: Timed client database assignment
challenges.scenario: Complete a client request from requirements to query, validation, interpretation and handoff.
challenges.tasks: In 90 minutes, build a department medication-utilisation summary, a no-order encounter exception list, a data-quality report and a concise handoff. Include SQL, result exports, assumptions and limitations.
challenges.starter: Use client-brief.md, rubric.json and synthetic seed data. Submit your own query file and evidence screenshots or CSV outputs.
challenges.acceptance: Minimum 80/100 rubric score, no critical grain/denominator errors, and all key counts reconcile.
challenges.safety: A technically correct query with misleading interpretation is not a successful deliverable.
